chunk_findings.detail: `ddflow.adapters.mcp_client` imports several names from `.mcp` (`CLOSED_BEFORE_READ`, `ECHOED`, `EOF`, `ERROR`, `OFFER_VERSION`, `OK`, `POLL_S`, `TIMEOUT`, `UNAVAILABLE`, `Negotiation`, `describe_answer`, `encode`, `initialize_request`, `negotiate`, `request`, `response_in`), but `ddflow.adapters.mcp` is being split and reduced in size. If `ddflow.adapters.mcp` no longer exports these names or if `ddflow.adapters.mcp` itself needs to import items from `mcp_client`, this will create a circular import at runtime when any module imports `ddflow.adapters.mcp` (which re-exports everything from `mcp_client` according to the module docstring). Given that `mcp` imports nothing from `mcp_client` in the provided diff while `mcp_client` imports from `mcp`, any attempt by `mcp` to re-export `McpClient`, `StdioClient`, or related types defined in `mcp_client.py` will fail due to a circular import when `mcp` is imported before `mcp_client` is fully initialized, or will raise an `ImportError` if those names are not explicitly re-exported in `ddflow/adapters/mcp.py` (which is not shown as modified to add re-exports).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/mcp_client.py:41

chunk_findings.detail: The move deletes the public helper `send_line` from `ddflow.adapters.mcp` and the re-export list does not bring it back (only `Channel`, `Handshake`, `McpClient`, `Outcome`, `Starter`, `StdioClient`, `_ChannelClient`, `finish_answer`). The comment says those imports exist so existing `from ddflow.adapters.mcp import ...` sites, including the ACP client that shared this plumbing, keep resolving. `from ddflow.adapters.mcp import send_line` therefore raises `ImportError` after this change; it succeeded before, and `_ChannelClient._send` was the caller of that helper.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/mcp.py:329

chunk_findings.detail: `StdioClient.connect` assigns `self._channel = self._starter(...)` without closing an existing channel. A second `connect` (retry after timeout, or a caller that reconnects) drops the first `Channel` with no `close()`, so that server process keeps running; later `close()` only stops the replacement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/mcp_client.py:153

chunk_findings.detail: After a successful `initialize`, `notifications/initialized` is sent with raw `json.dumps`, while every request in `_exchange` is sent with `encode` (the wire framing this module is not supposed to reimplement). A newline- or content-length-framed server therefore never sees a complete initialized frame: the next `tools/list` line is glued to the notification, the handshake never finishes, and `list_tools` returns `TIMEOUT` even though `initialize` already succeeded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/mcp_client.py:167

chunk_findings.detail: `connect` assigns `self._channel = self._starter(...)` without closing an existing channel. A second `connect` (retry after `TIMEOUT`/`EOF`, or a caller that reconnects) drops the only reference to the first `Channel` and never calls `close`, so the first server process keeps running. `close` is the only method that stops a server, and nothing else in this module retains that channel.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/mcp_client.py:StdioClient.connect

chunk_findings.detail: The initialized notification is the only outbound frame not passed through `encode`. `_exchange` sends `encode(frame)` (the line framing this module says lives in `encode`); `connect` sends `json.dumps({... notifications/initialized ...})` with no delimiter. On a newline-delimited MCP stdio channel whose `send` writes the string as given, that notification is glued to the next `tools/list`/`tools/call` line, so the server never completes `notifications/initialized` and cannot parse the following request; `list_tools` then returns `TIMEOUT` (or `ECHOED`) even though initialize succeeded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/mcp_client.py:StdioClient.connect
